newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen opening higher with bonds.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen opening higher with bonds.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to head higher at the start of trading on Thursday after a larger than expected weekly jobless claims number rallied the bond market.
Analysts said the Dow could make a stab at the 6700 level before running into some profit-taking. The long bond was up 13/32 to yield 7.06 percent.

"It looks like we are headed for a positive opening," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments. "The bond market is up, and the long bond yield is approaching seven percent. That will give a boost to stocks."

Weekly jobless claims rose to 332,000 from the previous week's revised 324,000. The U.S. February trade deficit narrowed by 8.5 percent to $11.59 billion from the previous month's revised $12.67 billion.

"The basic fundamentals remain positive," Cardillo said. "Earnings are coming in better than expected, and you can't ask for more than that. Business is good, and the market will reach for 6700. We will some selling as we approach it."
The Philadelphia Federal Reserve survey is due out at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT.
